corrections.form_value: Three outcomes: S1-O1 novelty rating, S1-O2 surprise rating, S1-O3 RQ count. The value and relevance ratings appear only inside the MANOVA mention.
corrections.source_says: Participants rated RQs on four aspects that the paper treats as creativity criteria: novelty, value, surprise, and relevance. The MANOVA F(4, 209) covers all four. Table 1 gives Condition (Depth-First=1) beta (S.E.) = 1.54 (.64)* for Value and 1.70 (.68)* for Relevance. Under form rule 7 these are two more outcomes scored on output (value as usefulness; relevance as usefulness or other), measure self_report, unit rating, direction treatment_higher.
corrections.quote: We adopt Boden’s criteria [3] to measure creativity from three different aspects- novelty, value, surprise, and relevance.

confirmed: Version facts: the margin stamp reads 'arXiv:2310.06155v3 [cs.HC] 20 Mar 2024', and the file has 25 pages (p. 1; p. 2, ACM reference '25 pages'; PyMuPDF page count). The arXiv API lists v3 as the latest version. The title on the document and the eight authors match p. 1.

Randomization: the assignment quote is verbatim (p. 9, Section 6.1; the PDF breaks 'counter-balanced' across a line). The order of the two designs and the two topics was randomized and counterbalanced. Codebook criterion 1 accepts a within-person design with randomized order, so criterion 1 met, unit within_person_order, and structure within are right.

has_randomized_people_study is true. In the one experiment, 20 HCI researchers each used two generative-AI configurations of CoQuest (breadth-first and depth-first, on a GPT-3.5 agent) in randomized order. The participants rated the research questions they co-created on novelty, value, surprise, and relevance, and the paper counts the questions by condition (p. 8, Section 6; p. 9, Sections 6.1, 6.2.1, 7.1.1). The formative study with four researchers has no AI condition (p. 4, Section 4).

design_class lab_rct fits: sessions were run remotely over video calls with screen sharing, lasted 1-2 hours, and paid $20 per hour (p. 8, Section 6). context_class none is right for a randomized experiment.

Counts: the participants quote is verbatim (p. 8, Section 6). The 20 HCI researchers came from 8 institutions and were all graduate students currently enrolled or just graduated (p. 8). The limitations call them doctoral students (p. 19, Section 9), so population students fits. All counts are people. The paper prints no count at assignment and no exclusions (participants were free to withdraw, p. 8). With 20 people analyzed, fewer than 50, criterion 2 not met and core no are correct.

Arms and tool: the breadth-first and depth-first descriptions match p. 6, Section 5.1.2, and Figure 4 (p. 7), with three RQs per turn in both designs (p. 6). AutoGPT, gpt3.5-turbo-16k, and text-embedding-ada-002 through Azure (p. 8, Section 5.2.3) and the ReAct framework (p. 7, Section 5.2.1) match ai_tool.name_model. The two topics and the duration match p. 8, Sections 6 and 6.1.

S1-O1 reported matches p. 10, Section 7.1.2: MANOVA F(4, 209) = 3.79, p = .0057**, Wilk's Λ = 0.909; novelty U = 2199.5, p = .002**, d = .40, Power = .89; depth-first M=3.78, SD=1.29 vs breadth-first M=3.28, SD=1.22. The bracketed caveat is correct: one M/SD pair follows both tests.
S1-O2 reported matches p. 10, Section 7.1.2: surprise U = 2387.5, p = 0.017*, d = .32, Power = .75, rated higher under depth-first.

S1-O3 reported matches p. 9, Section 7.1.1: 504 RQs in total, 276 (M=14.53, SD=6.19) under breadth-first and 228 (M=12, SD=5.31) under depth-first. No test of the RQ count by condition appears anywhere. Tables 1 and 2 use 'Total # of RQs Created' only as a predictor (p. 15), and the Mann-Whitney tests on p. 13 compare wait-time actions.

one_line_finding numbers are correct: the novelty and surprise tests (p. 10, Section 7.1.2) and the survey creativity result U = 288.0, p = .015, d = .68, breadth-first M=3.78 (SD=0.82) vs depth-first M=3.18 (SD=0.69) (pp. 9-10, Section 7.1.1). Leaving the survey score out of the outcomes is right: its creativity items mix a rating of the generated RQs with how creative participants felt (p. 22, Appendix A.1, Table 3).
criterion_3 unclear is defensible: the RQ ratings come from the participants themselves (p. 9, Section 6.2.1), and the RQ count counts AI-generated questions.

preregistered not_stated is right (no mention in the paper). company_involvement false is right: funding is NSF Grant No. 2119589 and CloudBank, NSF award 1925001 (p. 19, Acknowledgments). The paper names no other paper that uses these participants.

Audit note, not a form error: the per-person RQ means equal 276/19 = 14.53 and 228/19 = 12.0, not 276/20 = 13.8 and 228/20 = 11.4, so the per-person counts may cover 19 participants although the paper says 20 (p. 9, Section 7.1.1). The Table 1 depth-first coefficients (1.52 to 1.70 points, p. 15) are also much larger than the 0.50 gap between the printed means (3.78 vs 3.28, p. 10), and the paper does not reconcile the two.
summary: The form codes the design correctly (20 HCI graduate researchers used two GPT-3.5 CoQuest designs in randomized, counterbalanced order, a small randomized experiment with core no), and every number it records matches pp. 9-10. It misses Table 1 on p. 15, which gives depth-first coefficients with standard errors for all four RQ ratings, so the value and relevance outcomes and the novelty and surprise standard errors are absent and statistics_available is empty; the code URL, the design summary, one locator quote, the version label, and the appendix field need smaller fixes.
